frequency_question: How often do bills requiring documentary proof of citizenship or similar contested federal mandates pass the U.S. Senate within a comparable window?
membership_rule: Members are standalone major election or immigration restriction bills that faced filibuster thresholds and partisan opposition; excluded are must-pass omnibus appropriations, routine extensions, or uncontroversial bipartisan measures.

cases.name: Border Security, Economic Opportunity, and Immigration Modernization Act (2013 - passed Senate, died in House)
CLEAR Act / various state-ID companion measures
For the People Act (S. 1 - 2021 cloture vote)
Freedom to Vote Act (2022 cloture vote)

coverage_note: 7 named major partisan bills; captures the structural difficulty of breaking the 60-vote filibuster threshold for standalone controversial election/citizenship bills.
known_gaps: Excludes minor committee-only marker bills that never received a chamber-wide test.
skeleton: 7 identified legislative attempts of high-salience, highly partisan electoral/citizenship bills in divided or narrow-majority Senates over nearly two decades.
multiplier: 1 out of 7 passed the Senate floor.
validity_reason: Valid through the current congressional alignment; would only reset if the filibuster rule itself is abolished or significantly altered.
